name: Week 23 KB Tuesday — NEW: Long Coordination Gauntlet (14-Move Conti Flow) 🌀 + Figure-8 Switch-Clean Warmup
description:
Tuesday's the day for the big one. The **Long Coordination Gauntlet** — a fourteen-move continuous Conti flow that has never been run — takes the main slot. It's leg-athletic and long, which is exactly why it belongs on Tuesday, three clear days from Friday legs.

And the move you've been missing comes back where you wanted it: the **figure-8 → switch → tactical clean** opens the warmup as a brain-primer. It's the hand-switch figure-8 that cleans, not the marching one and not the continuous weave — the one you sneak in yourself because it works your head.

**Warmup reminder:** figure-8 switch-clean drill → halo → bottoms-up press (18lb) → internal core fist rotation → protective behind-back shrug, then the 7-move banded prep.

Strict press holds 50, front squat covers the squat pattern. Structure keeps the strength block before the big flow so it's not top-heavy.

spotlights.why: This is the move you asked for by name — the hand-switch figure-8 that exits into a tactical clean, the one that 'works your brain.' It's back as a warmup because that's where a pure coordination drill belongs: low load, full attention, priming the hand-eye and the cross-body pattern before the gauntlet asks for it twice. The spotlight is on owning the switch cleanly — the bell passes between the legs, the hands trade, and it comes up into the clean in one arc with no reset. Get it smooth here and the gauntlet's version feels like an old friend.

The technical crux of the gauntlet and probably the least familiar move in the whole KB library for you — it closes the fourteen-move chain, which means it arrives when you're most fatigued and least sharp. That's the point of spotlighting it: not to muscle it, but to know it's coming and give it a light bell and full respect. If the catch feels off, slow the whole chain down going into it rather than rushing to finish.

Every week pulls at least one thing off the bench.

sets.name: 🔆 Warm-Up — Figure-8 Switch-Clean Brain-Primer + Cuff Prep

exercises.notes:
**🔆 SPOTLIGHT (warmup slot) — the move you missed, as a brain-primer. LOAD:** 18-26lb, light.
- **The hand-switch figure-8 that cleans** — bell passes between the legs, hands trade, comes up into a tactical clean in ONE arc, no reset
- **Stay low, wide stance** through the figure-8; drive the clean from the hips
- Low load, full attention — this is a coordination drill, not a strength set. Own the switch and it primes the gauntlet's version
**LOAD:** 15-20lb. Big slow circles both directions — open the shoulders.
**LOAD:** 18lb. Inverted bell over a vertical forearm, grip hard, shoulder packed. 8/side forward + T-plane (T-plane light). Cuff prep.
Standing, hinged slightly forward. Tight fists, thumbs tucked — grip + forearm primer for a long single-bell day.

exercises.equipment: light DB pair or a KB held behind the body
exercises.notes: **Protective shrug (greasing set).** 1 light set held behind the body, palms back. Pack DOWN and BACK, shrug UP and slightly back, 1s squeeze, slow down.

sets.name: Banded Shoulder Prep (~3 min)

exercises.notes: Mini-band OR blue rope band held in hands.
Elbows drive to the ribs, scaps depress.
Don't overarch the lower back to chase range.
15s each side — primes the overhead + rotation the gauntlet's snatches and presses need.
Both arms in a V/Y, hold and breathe. Lower traps fire.

sets.notes: 1 round of all 7 banded moves (~3 min). Sustained tension, no rest between positions.

sets.name: Strength — Strict Press + Front Squat (Before the Gauntlet) 🛑

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 50 across all sets — strict single-arm press, clean to rack, press straight up, NO push-press. 8/8/8 is the standard you hold.
- **Strict, ribs DOWN**, no rib flare
- **Bicep finishes by the ear, full lockout, pack the shoulder DOWN**
- Both sides to the same standard

**LOAD:** 25-35lb racked.
- **Sit tall, full depth, no bounce** out of the bottom
- **Ribs down, brace** — the racked bell pulls you forward; stay upright
- Drive up through the whole foot. Leg-athletic on Tuesday is fine

sets.notes: 3 rounds, strength before the flow so the day isn't top-heavy. Strict press is the anchor; front squat covers the squat pattern.

sets.name: 🌀 Long Coordination Gauntlet (NEW — 14-Move Conti Flow)
sets.notes:
**Single LIGHT bell (~18-26lb), 2 full rounds each side.** Brand new, and the longest chain in the program — fourteen moves, run the whole thing on one side before switching.

**This is a LEARNING run.** The win today is knowing the order and hitting clean transitions, not moving fast or heavy. Keep the flow card open; expect to stall and re-check the sequence the first round — that's what the second round is for.

**The chain mixes everything:** swings, cleans, the figure-8 switch-clean (twice — the move you love), thruster, windmills, lateral + curtsy lunge, overhead press, lunge snatch, skier swing, and the walter catch to close.

🛑 **Overhead + ballistic — keep it shy, the packed shoulder is the cap.** Pack DOWN on every press and snatch; the windmills come from the hips, not the arm. Go light and let the chain teach itself.

**The walter catch closes it** and it's the least familiar move — it arrives when you're most fatigued. If the catch feels off, slow the whole chain going into it rather than rushing to finish.

**Reflection:** which of the fourteen transitions breaks the chain — where do you stop and re-grip? Those seams are next week's skill. And does the figure-8 switch-clean feel like the old friend you've been sneaking in?

exercises.notes: 60s each side. Hip flexor release — counters the lunges, snatches, and thrusters.
60s. Adductors + inner hips — the figure-8's wide stance and the lateral lunges bill here.

🛑 **The walter catch closes the gauntlet** — least familiar move, most fatigued moment. Light bell; slow the chain into it if the catch feels off.
**Strict overhead press holds 50 at 8/8/8** — strict, no push-press.
**Front squat 25-35lb racked** — sit tall, full depth.
**Why Tuesday:** the gauntlet is leg-athletic and long, so it's free three days clear of Friday legs.
**Strength runs before the gauntlet** so the demanding volume isn't stacked at the top.
**Protective behind-back shrug greasing set in the warm-up.**
Rotation ahead: W24 brings back the B-Stance Flow (unseen since W11) + the Leggy Flow.
formPhilosophy: The gauntlet is here because a fourteen-move chain is the opposite of a stale week — it's more skill than you can hold in your head on the first pass, which is exactly what makes it worth running. And the move you kept sneaking in on your own finally has an official home, as a warmup, because that's what it is: a coordination primer that wakes up the hand-eye system before the real work. Both choices come from the same place — the KB days should be the part of the week you look forward to, and the way you keep them that way is to keep emptying the bench instead of re-running the same chain until it goes gray. Build the skills, keep it light, keep it fun. Building decades, not weeks.
